title: Federal bar on employing certain persons with access to controlled substances
rule_summary: The registrant shall not employ, as an agent or employee who has access to controlled substances, any person who has been convicted of a felony offense relating to controlled substances or who, at any time, had an application for registration with the DEA denied, had a DEA registration revoked or has surrendered a DEA registration for cause. For purposes of that provision, for cause means a surrender in lieu of, or as a consequence of, any federal or state administrative, civil or criminal action resulting from an investigation of the individual's handling of controlled substances.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate knows the federal hiring bar that binds every DEA-registered pharmacy, including the felony conviction and surrender-for-cause limbs and the access condition.
common_confusions: The bar reaches an agent or employee who has access to controlled substances, so the scope of the person's access is part of the test.
The federal bar adds a felony drug conviction and a surrender for cause, which the Massachusetts Department provision does not mention.
verification_notes: Read in the current eCFR text of 21 CFR 1301.76(a) on ecfr.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
